items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee discusses Willie's time with Duke Ellington and Harry James, and mentions Norman 'was a good friend of Willie', but the interviewee (Trummy Young) does not describe a direct personal relationship with Willie himself, only narrating third-party connections.

ctx.x: A lot of his friends said -- have told me all kinds of superstitious things.

He had a lot of hangups. He didn't have as many back there with Lunceford as he finally got later on, but he had -- he had some going for himself. Yeah, he had superstitions going, but he got an awful lot more hangups after he left Lunceford, I think. When he got with James he got more than he ever had before. And with Duke he had a lot of them too.

And Duke didn't want Willie to leave. But Duke told us once that he's just learning what Willie was doing to write right for him just before he left, you know. Because he had a good spot with Duke. You know, Duke would write for you. That's one thing. If you stayed with Duke long enough for him to see what your style was, he would write for you. Because he wrote for all the guys in that band.
